findings.message: The no-engine route says pause/resume 'acquire the same writer lock and apply directly under section 20's contract' and must 'never leave a request to act on an unrelated later lifecycle'. Section 20 only says 'the pre-daemon path is unchanged', but no pre-daemon pause/resume verb exists: the current parser has none, as the ticket itself notes. The pause projection is also lifecycle-bound (ControlInbox._fold accepts only decisions whose lifecycle_id matches its own), and with no engine running there is no lifecycle. The spec never says what a direct pause or resume writes or changes. It could journal a CONTROL_DECISION, and if so under which lifecycle_id and request_id. It could create a lifecycle. It could refuse, as direct kill does. It also never says whether a direct pause holds the next drain. test_pause_resume_apply_directly_under_lock ('direct behavior and no deferred request') therefore has no observable to assert, and the implementer would have to invent the record.
findings.paved_road: Harden 19.P3.pause-resume-activation (section 11.4) so it names the direct no-engine behavior exactly. Give either the journaled record (writer, envelope, body including lifecycle_id/request_id, and whether a later drain lifecycle folds it), or a lock-only refusal with its message and paved road, as section 20 does for kill. Then re-author this ticket's Records/Observable and that test's obligation from the plan text.

findings.message: The entry requires the active.json discovery record to be written through chupa/control.py's filesystem-seam writer, refreshed after each decision, and 'retired before releasing the lock' on exit, failure, cancellation and handoff. The FileSystem seam in chupa/seams.py offers only publish (no-overwrite), write and replace; it has no remove or unlink. The closed record shape {lifecycle_id, hold_id} has no retired form. So retirement either needs a new seam operation in chupa/seams.py, plus the test fakes such as ScriptFS, which is outside the scope fence, or needs a retirement representation the plan does not state. Calling Path.unlink directly would break the injectable-seam rule.
findings.paved_road: Harden 19.P3.pause-resume-activation to state the retirement mechanism. Either add a named FileSystem seam delete operation and put chupa/seams.py (and any fake implementing the protocol) in this ticket's Scope fence and Context, or specify a retirement representation reachable through existing seam operations, along with how publishers treat it. Then update the fence and the test_control_lifecycle_cleanup_on_exit_and_handoff obligation to match.

findings.message: Scope in requires phase3-continue-10 to cite 19.P3.kill-worker-stop and 19.P3.kill-failure-suppression, the payload units for phase3-continue-11. Following the phase3-continue-08 precedent, it also requires the successor to validate those units before writing. CHUPA_PLAN.md has no `### 19.P3.kill-worker-stop` or `### 19.P3.kill-failure-suppression` heading; the last Phase 3 entry units are kill-executor-abort (line 2005) and kill-signal-journal (line 2016). Section 13.3 refuses an unresolvable Plan contract id at the grammar gate, so the successor seed fails intake lint and requisition_review. That breaks criteria 1-3, and the implementer can only return premise_failed. The governing spec is missing two facts: the Owner/Records/Observable/Tests entry units for the kill-worker-stop and kill-failure-suppression registry rows.
findings.paved_road: Before re-running phase3-continue-09, harden the plan through section 11.4: add entry units `### 19.P3.kill-worker-stop` and `### 19.P3.kill-failure-suppression` after the existing kill units, carrying Owner, Records, Observable and Tests, and commit them. Then re-author this ticket with the successor's citations unchanged. Add those two units to this ticket's own Plan contract so its implementer can run entry_unit_gap and resolve_plan_contract on them directly.
